dish: House-made otōshi and home-cooked plates, famously the meat pie
n: Stand Suehiro, Sakaemachi (スタンド末広)
address: Ōyama Apartment 1F, 388-9 Asato, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
w: A small standing-style bar on the edge of Sakaemachi Market, named after the shokudō the owner's grandmother ran in Osaka. OTV's Sakaemachi bar-hop series calls its house-made otōshi the 'strongest' it found, and Smart Magazine singles out the meat pie as the popular order.

dish: Osaka-style kushikatsu (beef kushikatsu is the No.1 order) on a 4-item senbero set
n: Okinawa Kushikatsu Senbero-ya, Sakaemachi (沖縄串カツ せんべろ家)
w: A red-lantern kushikatsu counter inside Sakaemachi Market, sister shop of the bone-broth specialist Honejiru-ya. It fries Osaka-style kushikatsu and runs a 'senbero' set (4 items for ¥1,000); beef kushikatsu is the best seller, and OTV's Sakaemachi bar-hop series also praises its chicken wings.

dish: ¥50 mini croissants (sold in bags of ten) and a counter of sweet, savoury and hard breads
n: BOULANGERIE BZ, Yogi (ブーランジェリービズ)
w: A neighbourhood counter bakery in Yogi where staff fetch the breads you name. Its glazed mini croissants, ¥50 each and sold by the bag, are the famous item and are often reserved a day ahead; RETRIP and the local site TAGOO both list it among Naha's favourite bakeries.

dish: Ryūkyū court-style set courses (e.g. the 7-course Japanese-Ryūkyū menu) with live classical Ryūkyū dance
w: A ryōtei founded in 1949 in Tsuji, Naha's old entertainment quarter, now over 70 years old. Dinner is a set Ryūkyū or Japanese-Ryūkyū course served while professional dancers perform classical Ryūkyū dance. It holds the 'Ryūkyū ryōri ga ajiwaeru mise' certification and is listed by OCVB and Rurubu.

dish: Yaeyama-ryōri: traditional Yaeyama (Ishigaki) home and festive dishes made mostly with ingredients sent from Ishigaki
n: Yaeyama Ryōri Kotōzan Tantei, Shuri (八重山料理 虎頭山 潭亭)
w: A reservation-only Yaeyama-cuisine restaurant on Torazuyama hill in Shuri, looking out over Naha and Shuri Castle. Most ingredients come from Ishigaki, and the owner does every step of the cooking. It is a certified Ryūkyū-cuisine shop and is profiled by OCVB, Tabirai and Okinawa Traveler.

dish: Rafute braised in white miso, jīmāmi-dōfu (peanut tofu) and mimigā-style minudaru (sesame-crusted steamed pork)
n: Shuzen Maeda, Kume (酒膳 眞榮田)
w: A small Ryūkyū-cuisine dining bar in Kume holding the 'Ryūkyū ryōri ga ajiwaeru mise' certification. Okinawa Traveler's feature on the certified shops recommends its white-miso rafute, jīmāmi-dōfu and minudaru, a court-cuisine dish of pork steamed in a black-sesame crust.

n: Arakaki Chinsukō Honpo, Kokusai-dōri Makishi (新垣ちんすこう本舗 牧志店)
w: The Kokusai-dōri shop of the old Ryūkyū confectioner whose line goes back to Arakaki Shukiki, a royal-kitchen cook at Shuri Castle. Its founder is credited with turning chinsukō from a steamed cake into the baked biscuit sold today, and the shop still makes it by hand. Listed by OCVB, Mapple and Rurubu.

dish: Sātā andāgī, pōpō and mūchī; the auspicious nū-manjū (red-stamped bean bun)
w: A family confectioner more than 70 years old off Kokusai-dōri, selling everyday Okinawan sweets: sātā andāgī, pōpō crepe rolls, mūchī and the celebratory nū-manjū. OTV's Okitive profiles it as a long-standing shop, and Rurubu lists it.

dish: Tulip-shaped sātā andāgī made with eggs from the family's own Amuro poultry farm
n: Sātā Andāgī no Mise Amuro, Shuri (さーたーあんだーぎーの店 安室 首里平良店)
w: A sātā andāgī shop in Shuri run off the Amuro poultry farm, whose fresh eggs give the doughnuts a light, fluffy inside and a split 'tulip' top. Feel Japan lists it among Okinawa's nine must-try sātā andāgī shops, and Rurubu lists the Shuri Taira shop.

dish: Five house craft beers brewed on site: pale ale, IPA, stout, pilsner and weizen
n: KANEHIDE CRAFT BREWERY, Asahi-machi (カネヒデクラフトブルワリー)
address: Kanehide Building West 1F, 112-1 Asahi-machi, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
w: A small brewery and taproom run by the Okinawan Kanehide group on the ground floor of its office building, about five minutes from Asahibashi Station and the Naha Bus Terminal. Okinawa Times covered its opening, when it began brewing under a 2022 licence, and OCVB lists the taproom. Weekday evenings only.

dish: Okinawa soba in a clear pork-bone-and-bonito broth; mild miso-seasoned champurū
w: A neighbourhood shokudō in the residential streets behind Wakasa beach, serving Okinawan home cooking. Its champurū is seasoned with miso for a gentle taste, and the clear soup of pork bone and bonito is its most praised point. Listed by OCVB, Mapple and Rurubu.

dish: Champurū and Okinawa soba teishoku; all-you-can-eat curry
n: Taishū Shokudō Ikariya, Maejima (大衆食堂 いかり屋)
address: Okinawa Sailors Hall 1F, 3-25-50 Maejima, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
w: A big-menu harbour canteen on the ground floor of the seafarers' hall by Tomarin port, cooking champurū, Okinawa soba and Japanese, Western and Chinese plates. Okinawa Times' 'driver's meals' series covered its all-you-can-eat curry, and Ryukyu Shimpo and OTV both profile it as a lunch-and-dinner local favourite.

dish: Yaki-tebichi (pan-grilled pig's trotters, crisp outside and gelatinous inside, about an hour to order) and oden
n: Oden Tōdai, Sakaemachi (おでん東大) — CLOSED
w: A late-night oden bar in the Sakaemachi quarter that ran for about 70 years. It was famous for yaki-tebichi, pig's trotters grilled to order in a frying pan, which took over an hour to arrive. It closed on 26 September 2022, and Ryukyu Shimpo reported the loss of a Sakaemachi institution. Kept here, flagged closed, as part of the area's history.

dish: 'Mochiage': fish bought downstairs (e.g. irabuchā parrotfish) cooked to order as sashimi, garlic-butter sauté or soy-simmered, ¥500 cooking fee
n: Kiraku, Makishi Public Market 2F (きらく 第一牧志公設市場)
address: 2F Naha City Daiichi Makishi Public Market, 2-10-1 Matsuo, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
w: One of the upstairs restaurants of the rebuilt Makishi Public Market that carries on the market's 'mochiage' custom. You buy up to three kinds of fish or meat from the stalls on the ground floor and Kiraku cooks them for a ¥500 fee, for example parrotfish as sashimi, in garlic butter or simmered in soy. Ryukyu Shimpo walked through the system with its manager, and co-trip's market guide covers the mochiage experience.

dish: Craft beers brewed with Okinawan fruit: Sakurazaka Pale Ale (kābuchī citrus), Weizen (guava), Stout (coffee)
n: Sakurazaka Brewery, Makishi (桜坂ブルワリー)
w: A microbrewery at the foot of the Sakurazaka slope, five minutes' walk from Kokusai-dōri, that mostly brews with Okinawan fruit. Its core beers are a pale ale with kābuchī citrus, a guava weizen and a coffee stout. OCVB's Okinawa craft-brewery tour features it, and Feel Japan lists it among Naha's local breweries and bars.
